components.cost_effect: No actual initialization observations; matrix storage and linear algebra are separately charged.
components.goal: Keep the precision matrix invertible before sufficient real observations exist.
components.key_estimate: A_t is positive definite since A_t=A_1+sum_{s<t}x_s x_s^T and A_1 is positive definite.
components.name: Spanner initialization and accumulated least squares
components.operation: Initialize A with sum_i b_i b_i^T, then add x_t x_t^T and l_t x_t to the matrix and response statistic.

transfer_checks: Changing the spanner or regularizer requires a new calibration argument; invertibility alone does not prove coverage.

limitations.scope: Printed rule and unrestricted delta in (0,1)
limitations.statement: The printed all-time coverage is not accepted on the full input domain. Local consistency check: n=1,D={1},b_1=1,mu=1 and deterministic cost 1 satisfy the model. At delta=0.9, A_1=1,muhat_1=0 and beta_1=[(8/3)ln(10/9)]^2<1, so mu is outside B_1 before any observation. No performance guarantee is imported from that claim.
Exact optimistic selection is a distinct optimization task; one scalar observation per round does not imply computational efficiency or an unrestricted Oracle Complexity result.

variants.cost: Exactly one actual scalar bandit observation per round, hence T observations through horizon T. Spanner acquisition and exact optimistic minimization are separate computational resources. A dense direct implementation can store A_t and s_t in O(n^2) space and perform a matrix inversion/solve each round; this bookkeeping is not an efficiency claim for the optimistic minimization. The source's §3.4 distinguishes finite enumeration from potentially difficult general-domain optimization. No linear-optimization-oracle call bound is asserted for ConfidenceBall2.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.3 §2; p.4 Algorithm 3.1 and explanatory text; p.6 §3.4
variants.name: Printed ConfidenceBall2, Algorithm 3.1
variants.output: The online actions x_1,...,x_T in D, observed scalar losses and maintained estimates/confidence sets. The source does not prescribe an averaged or final recommendation for simple-regret optimization.
public_inputs: Dimension n>=1, compact full-rank D subset R^n, confidence input 0<delta<1, and an exact barycentric spanner b_1,...,b_n in D.
variants.query_and_update: At integer t>=1 set beta_t=max{128 n ln(t) ln(t^2/delta),[(8/3)ln(t^2/delta)]^2}; define B_t={nu in R^n:(nu-muhat_t)^T A_t(nu-muhat_t)<=beta_t}. Choose x_t in argmin_{x in D} min_{nu in B_t} nu^T x, incur and observe l_t=c_t(x_t). Set s_t=s_{t-1}+l_t x_t, A_{t+1}=A_t+x_t x_t^T and muhat_{t+1}=A_{t+1}^{-1}s_t. Any measurable minimizer may be selected when tied.
variants.requirements: For every history H_t and x in D, c_t(x) is in [-1,1] and E[c_t(x)|H_t]=mu^T x for fixed unknown mu. Only the chosen scalar cost is observed. Every x in D has spanner coefficients in [-1,1]. Exact optimistic optimization over D is available as a mathematical operation; efficient implementation is not assumed.
variants.state_and_initialization: A_1=sum_{i=1}^n b_i b_i^T, s_0=0 and muhat_1=0. The spanner is linearly independent, so A_1 is positive definite. Its contribution corresponds to fictitious zero-loss observations, not n actual bandit queries.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use natural logarithms and the displayed beta_t without modification. The printed loop runs indefinitely; an externally specified horizon T means retaining its first T rounds. No calibration repair, restart or accuracy-based stopping rule is introduced.
